The Bear Competitions Cookstown 100 is the oldest and opening Irish national road race of the 2026 season. Held on the 2.1-mile Orritor Circuit near Cookstown, Co. Tyrone, the 104th edition features practice on Friday and 18 races on Saturday including the Grand Final Open (A) race. Attracts top road racing talent from across Ireland and beyond.
Venue Address: Orritor Road, Cookstown, Co. Tyrone, BT80 9LX, Northern Ireland
Tags: Irish Road Racing, Road Race, Northern Ireland, Cookstown, National

Description: Ireland's largest outdoor sporting event and one of the world's fastest road races. The 2026 Briggs Equipment North West 200 runs on the iconic 8.9-mile Triangle circuit linking Portrush, Portstewart and Coleraine on the stunning Causeway Coast. Race week runs 4–9 May with practice on Wed 6 May, evening races Thu 7 May, and the main race day Sat 9 May. Top speeds exceed 200mph. Attracts 150,000+ spectators.
Venue Address: Portrush / Portstewart / Coleraine, Co. Antrim / Co. Londonderry, Northern Ireland
Tags: Irish Road Racing, Road Race, Northern Ireland, North West 200, International, NW200

Description: The return of the Kells Road Races to the 2.2-mile Crossakiel circuit after a 4-year absence due to insurance challenges in the Republic of Ireland. One of the most popular events in the Irish road racing calendar, held in Co. Meath with practice on Saturday 20 June and racing on Sunday 21 June. Part of the historic revival of road racing in the Republic of Ireland in 2026.
Host Name: Kells and District Motor Cycle Racing Club
Tags: Irish Road Racing, Road Race, Republic of Ireland, Kells, Meath

Description: The Around-A-Pound Tandragee 100 returns to the 5.3-mile course between Tandragee and Markethill in Co. Armagh, Northern Ireland. Practice on Friday 26 June (roads close 11am–9pm) and racing on Saturday 27 June (roads close 9.30am–7pm). Often described as a 'mini TT', the twisty and fast-flowing course is a favourite with riders and spectators alike. Regularly attracts competitors from around the world.
Venue Address: Tandragee, Co. Armagh, BT62, Northern Ireland
Host Name: North Armagh Motorcycle & Car Club Ltd.
Tags: Irish Road Racing, Road Race, Northern Ireland, Tandragee, Armagh

Description: The legendary Skerries 100 returns to Co. Dublin for the first time since 2022, making a hugely anticipated comeback as road racing revives in the Republic of Ireland. Hosted by the Loughshinny Motorcycle Supporters Club, the event runs over the weekend of 4–5 July 2026, taking in the roads of Skerries, a popular seaside town north of Dublin. One of Ireland's most iconic road racing events.
Tags: Irish Road Racing, Road Race, Republic of Ireland, Skerries, Dublin

Event Name: Walderstown Road Races 2026 – Race of the South
Description: The Walderstown 'Race of the South' returns to Co. Westmeath for the first time since 2022, hosted by the Fore Motorcycle Racing Club. Taking place on the Walderstown circuit on 18–19 July 2026, the event is a highlight of the Republic of Ireland's revived road racing calendar. Organised in partnership with the Faugheen 50 Supporters Club who generously offered their July dates to make the event possible.
Tags: Irish Road Racing, Road Race, Republic of Ireland, Walderstown, Westmeath

Event Name: Bayview Hotel Armoy Road Races 2026 – Race of Legends
Description: The Bayview Hotel Armoy Road Races – 'Race of Legends' – returns to the village of Armoy in Co. Antrim for 2026, running 24–25 July. Held in tribute to the famous Armoy Armada of Joey Dunlop, Mervyn Robinson, Frank Kennedy and Jim Dunlop, the race was first held in 2009 and is one of the most eagerly anticipated events on the Irish road racing calendar. Previous winners include Michael Dunlop, Davey Todd and Ryan Farquhar.
Venue Address: Armoy, Co. Antrim, BT53, Northern Ireland
Tags: Irish Road Racing, Road Race, Northern Ireland, Armoy, Antrim, Race of Legends

Description: The Mid Antrim 150 makes a welcome return to the 3.5-mile Clough circuit in Co. Antrim for the first time since 2022, running 31 July–1 August 2026. The event received official MCUI clearance following a successful course inspection and serves as the season finale of the Northern Ireland national road racing championship. A hugely popular event backed by strong community support.
Tags: Irish Road Racing, Road Race, Northern Ireland, Mid Antrim 150, Clough, Antrim

Description: The South West Road Races at Athea, Co. Limerick make a long-awaited return as road racing revives in the Republic of Ireland in 2026. Running 12–13 September, this is set to be the final Irish road race of the 2026 season. Organised by the South West Road Racing Club and held in the village of Athea in Co. Limerick, it rounds off a landmark year for the sport in Ireland.
Tags: Irish Road Racing, Road Race, Republic of Ireland, Athea, Limerick
